utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. Before the witness is being brought in, the Chamber would like to raise a procedural matter. Mr. Tolimir submitted on the 22nd of March his motion for an extension of the dead-line for filing a response to the Prosecution's motion for an order requiring the accused to provide sufficient particulars of his alibi defence. The motion was filed in English yesterday, and the Prosecution managed to respond already yesterday. The Prosecution doesn't object to this request. The Chamber would like to issue a decision on this request orally. The Chamber has reviewed Mr. Tolimir's request for a postponement of the dead-line to the 12th of April to file a response to the Prosecution's motion. It notes that the justification provided by the accused for this request is his need to focus on witnesses appearing in court, analysis of recently-disclosed material, and issues raised by the Prosecution's motion. The Chamber is of the view that the request of Mr. Tolimir is justified. The motion to exceed the time-limit for the response is granted. The response should be filed by the 12th of April, 2010. Thank you. The witness should be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please sit down. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to remind you that the solemn declaration you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Mr. Tolimir has some further questions for you. Please, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. God's peace, and I bless all in the courtroom and all of those following the proceedings, and all those to whom these proceedings refer to in any way. I would like to welcome the witness and continue where we left off.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Defence please play a video recording, 1D024. This is video footage that was recorded with amateur camera, and it's the review of the 28th Division in Srebrenica on the day of the forming of the staff of the forces in Srebrenica in May 1994. This is part of the 8th Operations Group of Srebrenica, which is part of the 2nd Corps of the B and H Army. Since the witness was a member of that armed formation, he can perhaps provide information that is important for these proceedings before this Trial Chamber. The video footage has been partially transcribed. Those parts are transcribed that we will be using in the courtroom, to the extent we require, in order to understand this video material. Even though the pictures are enough, we hope it will not be necessary to show the entire footage, but only certain excerpts. The entire footage is 43 minutes' long. We're going to show just portions of it to see when this footage was created. Could we please play it from the beginning, from the beginning to 0.59 seconds. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I didn't turn on the mike.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: First of all, you were a member of the 28th Division. This is indisputable, from your previous statements and testimony here, in the prior period and in previous testimony, so we will not dwell on that. First, can you identify and tell us the first and last name of the person reading out this order by Naser Oric, commanding certain soldiers. We will identify the others later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was not at this review. I know that I was not there, definitely, because this was not an obligation. I don't know who was reading it. It was some of these clerks, so-called clerks, which is what they were referred to in Tito's army. I don't know. I wasn't there. All those who wanted to go there could go.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We're satisfied with your answer. You say you don't know about the name of that, so we hope that this will be recorded in the transcript. My second question is: What is implied with the expression "exceptional results achieved in combat"? Can you please explain that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really couldn't say. I'm not a combat expert, military expert. I don't know what that's about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us, since a large number of names are being mentioned, it's a long list of names being read out - there's no need for us to look at all of that in the courtroom - but can you please tell us whether you're familiar with the soldiers and officers who were commended on the second anniversary of this particular unit in Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about those who were commended. I know those who were in front. Ramiz was there, Naser. I know those people. I don't know the names; the names of the persons were read out, but the actual people were not shown, so I really do not know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, were you commended by Naser Oric? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive 10 days in prison because I was captured by the UNPROFOR in Buljim, and they captured my rifle. It wasn't my rifle, but it was the rifle of another soldier who was on the front-line, so this is what I received.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play the second segment of this video footage, which is important for me to be able to put certain questions to this witness. The video segment is about three, three and a half minutes long, and it's from 10 minutes, 10 seconds; to 13 minutes, 32 seconds. That would be the segment that we would need to play. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that we have not been given the transcript of this video footage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, sir, at the very beginning of this segment, it says: "Gentlemen, soldiers, officers, salute to the homeland." Am I correct if I say that on review here are soldiers and officers who have been invited to salute the homeland? Thank you. Sir, can you tell us whether soldiers and senior officers are in the review?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is only one half of the division that is being shown here, the number that are reviewed. I don't know who are the commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm asking you -- I didn't ask you if they were commanders. I'm just asking you if these were soldiers and officers of the 28th Division. Can you answer that, please.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can see is Naser and all of these people around him. I don't know any the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell this Trial Chamber here whether the soldiers and officers of the 28th Division were being reviewed here. Yes or no. We're not asking you anything else.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them probably were, yes, some of them. Those who were there were there. Those who were there were there. Those who weren't, weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All of those who were in the line, were they all members of the 28th Division? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what else can they be? They're not sheep. You can see that they're soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, thank you. Those who were not in uniform, were they wearing any insignia or any other kind of sign or marking?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, thank you. Can we play the video material, and then we will continue with our questions. Can we play the it from 30th minute to 16 seconds; to 39 minute, 7 seconds. This is a very long segment, but perhaps it is the most significant one, as far as questions I'm going to put to the witness are concerned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, sir, we have seen here two segments where the fighters of the 28th Division are in review. Can you tell us whether a large number of them are in civilian clothing or whether they're wearing uniforms. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In civilian clothing, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So most of them wore civilian clothing and not uniforms during combat? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any combat here. I see a review of troops, and people are wearing predominantly civilian clothing. I don't know anything about anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is a review of troops where they are being commended for their participation in combat in the Kladanj sector of the front, and Srebrenica, Zepa, and Vlasenica are part of the Kladanj front or the Kladanj sector; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was explaining what the Kladanj unit did in Kladanj, not what this unit did. This unit is being reviewed, but it didn't go into any combat. He was explaining what was happening in Kladanj, what the Kladanj unit had done. This is what he was explaining. You could hear that over the radio every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: He was explaining what the Kladanj unit did. But he was reading a commendation for results achieved in combat, and this is what he said, that soldiers are being commended for their achievements in battle. Do you agree with me or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which combat you're talking about. He didn't actually say for which combat actions they're being commended.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. He did not mention that, yes, but he did say that it was in combat. Thank you. Now, we saw here, and you can confirm for the Trial Chamber because they do not understand the language that we speak, that orders were given here and that before the image was frozen, they were discussing the events in the Kladanj front-line. Can you confirm that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had radios, and we could hear every day what was going on around Sarajevo, Tuzla, Kladanj, Olovo. So first he said that this was broadcast on the radio, and then that he also received information from the corps. One could hear, over the radio, daily what the unit had done in Kladanj or Sarajevo. We had that information on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the Kladanj unit actually your adjacent unit in your zone of operations and part of it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, they are quite apart. Kladanj is 200 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Which unit was closer to Vlasenica than your unit and the Kladanj unit? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So your units were the only ones who were actually in the area of responsibility in Vlasenica, so your unit and the Kladanj unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "operations in Vlasenica"? Well, first of all, there was the Milici and Srb towns. How could we have control over Vlasenica, which was behind these two towns. You couldn't even reach them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We will come to that and see what kind of control they had. Now, Witness, tell me, how frequent were these review of troops? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I probably attended one of them. This was a review of a company, but I didn't have time to go for reviews of divisions because I had a large plot of land, and I had to work on the land. I wasn't really very involved with all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you please tell the Trial Chamber, how can you actually differentiate between officers and regular soldiers when you observed this video?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really tell the difference at all because they were all in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, as a member of the 28th Division, did you have any kind of marking, any kind of patch or insignia that you wore, either in combat, in defence, or in reviews of troops like this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had nothing. The commander would come by the bunker or trench to see if anybody was wounded, in case we were in combat, to check whether we had enough ammunition, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you were an officer in this division. Could you tell this Trial Chamber, please, whether you're familiar with the provisions of the Geneva Conventions and whether you had undergone any type of training for Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never heard of Geneva Conventions, and I didn't know anything about that. And, in any case, if it was violated, the violations were on your side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well -- thank you. Well, would you please speak before this Court in the language that is appropriate for a courtroom and use those terms. Now, what is -- how could you tell that someone was an officer, and actually tell the difference between them and a regular soldier? You were, you said, a team leader, a squad leader, and could you tell me, what was the system whereby you could actually differentiate?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, there were no markings, no badges, no insignia, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was it possible in combat for the enemy to actually discern between soldiers and officers based on your clothes and your uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter would request that the questioner and the witness pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, as an officer, military officer at the time, are you familiar with an old rule of the Law on War, that it is necessary to differentiate -- to tell and to mark soldiers so that it is possible to differentiate between them and civilians?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If soldiers and civilians had the same kind of clothes, tell me, then, how was it possible -- in this period from 1992 to 1995, could you actually tell between a civilian who went scavenging for food and, for instance, a guard or someone who was on patrol, a soldier on patrol?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that. That's what your soldiers were supposed to differentiate in Potocari, between elderly men and children. I mean, I wouldn't know how to differentiate -- I don't know how they were differentiated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the next question: Can you confirm that able-bodied men in Srebrenica had military -- whether they were conscripts and whether they had to report if they received a call-up from their superior command or their commander?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably that was the case, as required.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please see the last portion of this video - it will be very brief - and then we will change topics and go to identification. This is from 39 minutes, 20 seconds; to 45 minutes, 15 seconds -- 41 minutes, 15 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In order to facilitate our work here, we have actually selected a few images from the video and made photographs out of them, because we are going to be dealing with these individuals frequently, so I would now appreciate it if these photos, these photo frames, could be shown to the witness so that he can help us to identify those individuals. Could we now please first pull up 1D46 on the monitors. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, could you please identify these three individuals that we can see in this frame?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please take that pencil and just write the initials of the individuals that you do know above them, above their heads. Thank you. And for those you don't know, just leave without any initials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment. The Court Officer will assist you. Everything is prepared.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. Could we now please admit this into evidence, this image with the markings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it reserved? The marking disappeared on the screen. It is reserved. That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D4, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please show the witness 1D47. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's Commander Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please write his initials, Mr. Naser Oric's initial, in a blank space that you can find on the photo. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D5, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness now be shown 1D48, please. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this person in the photograph? And could you tell us what his role in the BH Army in Srebrenica was. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about this photo. There is a man who looks like him a bit, but I don't know if that's him. I'm not sure, and I can't really write anything down because I'm not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Then why don't you just write "I don't know." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, we would like to know by the interpreters, what does "Neznam" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "I don't know," interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. This marked photo will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D6, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The "Neznam" means that the witness does not know the person depicted in the photo. Thank you. Could the witness now please be shown 1D49.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could the witness please tell the Trial Chamber if he knows who this person is and what his role in the BH Army was. Because we see that he was here in the company of the leading men of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. He may have been an interpreter with UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please write "I don't know" next to this person.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you tendering this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. I failed to switch on my microphone, so you couldn't hear my request. Please, I'd like to tender it into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The marked photo with the word "Neznam" will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D7, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness now please be shown 1D50. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, tell us, please, do you know these individuals in the photo? If you do, would you please put, to the right of their head, their initials. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who they are [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In that case, please just put the words "I don't know" next to this other individual as well.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this photo into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The photo is again marked in the same way and will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D8, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown 1D51. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us whether you know these two persons in the photo. If you do, would you please put their initials on the right-hand side of their -- of these -- of each individual. And if not, just write the words "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know them [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could the witness now tell us -- this is a bad -- poor photo, but could the witness tell us what type of patch this person on the right-hand side has on his sleeve?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I can see is a white patch, but I can't distinguish anything on it, no letter, no nothing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wish to tender this into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D9, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness now please be shown 1D52. Thank you. 1D52, please. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could the witness now please tell us who the individuals in the photos are, or, rather, who the individual to the right of Mr. Oric is and what his role in the 28th Division was. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a relative of mine, Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Are both of them Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the other person [marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wish to tender this photograph into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D10, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would appreciate if all these photos and the videotape, 1D0024, be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The photos are already tendered, and they are exhibited. Mr. Tolimir, could you tell us a little bit more about the video? Who took the video, and when was it taken; do you know? Can you give us some information?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This video footage was received from the Association of Serb Victims, and it was made by individuals in Srebrenica who were present during the review of troops of the 28th Division, where the commendations were read out. And in the first photo, we could see this individual because he was reading out the orders and the commendations. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: These three parts of the video will be received as one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D11, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would now like to show the witness 1D045. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us who is depicted in this photo and what type of weapons does he have. Could you write, to the right of him, his initials, and below would you please write the type of weapon, if you know, that he's carrying. And if you don't, just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question orally. We see you're marking, but perhaps you can explain it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honours. I apologise. This is Naser Oric, and he doesn't -- and he has an M-84 rifle. Actually, it's a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, and thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you tell us now, Witness, please, whether machine-guns were the type of weapon that had to be handed over to UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I don't even know when this photo was taken and whether UNPROFOR was already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you just tell me and answer my question, whether this weapon was actually subject to UNPROFOR obligations? And if not, we will just tender this into evidence. If you don't know the answer, just say so.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: My colleague has a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, on this photograph, you said that the person who is carrying this weapon is Naser Oric. 4D10, you also spoke of a Naser Oric who apparently is a parent in your family. Is it the same Naser Oric who is the commander of the 28th Division, or is it -- are they two different persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Naser was a commander. It's one person. All the photographs depict him. But I did make a mistake, if I can correct that. I wrote "OM." I should have written "ON." Actually, "OM" are my initials.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll let that stay in the transcript, if possible. Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Of course, that is recorded correctly. There can't be any mistake. The marked photo will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D12, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please show the witness photograph 1D43. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could the witness please look at the photograph carefully and to tell us whether this is some kind of unit, or an established unit, or people from one establishment unit, and whether these are members of the 28th Division, among whom is also Naser Oric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you please look at the faces on this photograph and tell us if you know any of the people in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot, really. The picture is very blurry. You cannot really see very well. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you please look at the young man who is to the right of Naser Oric. Do you know him, on the photograph? Who is that? As you are looking, it would be to the left.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please ask the usher to take the hard copy of the photograph to the witness - it's the same as the one on the screen - to see whether he can recognise the person whose face is circled and who is positioned to the right of Naser Oric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you do that, could the Chamber please see the photo, because you indicated that there's some markings on the photo. The photo, the hard copy -- the photo on the hard copy is different from the photo we see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please look at the photograph. It's the same photograph that we're looking at on the screen, except it's a hard copy, and you can compare the photograph on the screen and the photograph that is in hard copy. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is not the same photo. It might be the same photo, but you have added some markings, a circle around one head and some other markings, quite illegible. And, therefore, I think we must clarify the situation. If you want the witness to mark that person who should be, in your understanding, Naser Oric, you should ask him, Mr. Tolimir, first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, he recognised Naser Oric. I'm asking him to recognise the person to the right of Naser Oric. The person to the right of Naser Oric, I circled that person in red. And if the witness knows this person, I'm asking him to place the initials of that person above that person's head.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't even see Naser Oric on the picture on the screen. I cannot recognise any face that is on the screen. And I wrote on the screen "I don't know." I cannot tell who is who here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, I take it that you don't recognise anybody in the photo, and nobody seems to be Naser Oric, in your understanding. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't see that here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, Mr. Tolimir, I think it's not valid to show the hard copy with markings that stem from you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Do you permit me, then, at the next session to show the same photograph without the markings that I made, and then we can see whether the witness can recognise the person in question? I only marked the face to indicate to the witness which person I was interested in and which person he should look at to see if he recognises that person. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think there will be no problem if you have the identical photo in the hard copy without any markings. That can be prepared for the second session. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, first, are you tendering the admission of this photo on the screen with the marking?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I would like to tender this photograph, and I would like this -- the words that the witness wrote, "I don't know," to be part of that exhibit. I would like to save that on the photograph. Thank you. Since we have 20 minutes before the break, Your Honour, is it okay if we take a break 20 minutes earlier?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This marked photo on the screen will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D13, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I take it you want to have the first break now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you wish, we can take the break now and bring the photograph at the beginning of the next session. All we are doing, actually, is moving the break forward, if you are -- if you agree to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, we will adjourn now for our first technical break. We will resume at 10 minutes before 4.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We apologise for the delay. We were occupied by another matter. Please, Mr. Tolimir, continue with your questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to ask for the photograph now to be shown that we had asked the witness to look at earlier. This is D43, if it's clear. If not, then perhaps he can look at the actual hard copy. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, can you now clearly see the photograph, and do you recognise any of the persons that are on it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you recognise Naser Oric? Is that him in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you recognise these three people who are squatting in front of others? They are not standing, but they're squatting in the first row, one, two, three. In the middle, you see somebody that I am asserting is Naser, and then there are two people on each side -- or there's one person on each side of him. Do you recognise any of those two people?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm seeing them for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you write on the photograph that you do not recognise the person sitting to the right of Naser? Can you write, "I don't know," "I don't know," I don't know," or, "I don't recognise the person," "I don't recognise the person," "I don't recognise the person," three times below each of the persons boots. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, in your last question you suggested to the witness that the person in the middle is Naser Oric. He didn't say that. I just wanted to clarify that, and you now can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I confirm that he didn't say that. Yes, he said that he didn't recognise the person. That is why I said that he should write, "I don't know," underneath each of the three persons in the front. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you tender this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I would like to have this photograph tendered, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D14, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I would still like to look at 1D43. I would like to put one more question to you in relation to that photograph. Thank you. We're waiting for 1D43 to appear again. Thank you. Thank you. We see the photograph. Witness, please, do you at least recognise the weapons that these persons in the photograph are carrying? Do you know what kind of weapons they have? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see on the right, at the end, the man is holding an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And do you see any other weapons there? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Are all the persons in uniform? Are they wearing military uniforms and boots? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you see a hunting rifle on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know that on the 16th of July, 1995, you were recorded -- or on the 16th of July, 1995, in Nezuk? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm repeating the question. Do you happen to know that the camera recorded your image on the 16th of July, 1995, or on about that date, in Nezuk?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Still I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you recorded by a camera in Nezuk?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes or no, were you or weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please play 1D054. This is video material. This is the footage provided to us from the Prosecution, and I'm grateful to the Prosecution for disclosing this material to us. The footage shows members from the Srebrenica 28th Division after the breakthrough. Can we please play the material from 1 minute, 31 seconds; to 1 minute, 34 seconds, where it says: "Yes, there is ammunition. Very well, there is everything." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can you now freeze the frame at 03.24 to 3.25.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us whether this is you in the photograph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you recognise this person in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think your microphone was not activated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you please write on the photograph that you don't know these persons, if you don't know them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, you cannot write on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I'm told that the witness can't mark on this video. This is not possible. But we have it on the record, his comment. I think that is enough.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It's sufficient that this is recorded in the transcript, that the witness does not recognise the persons on the photograph or the frame that we are looking at right now. The film goes on for a few minutes longer. It's about 6 minutes long. If we stay with this witness for a little bit longer, we can save time later in the cross-examination of other witnesses because there will be no more need to look at the entire video footage, but only the frames from this video material. So I would like to put some more questions to the witness about this material. Thank you. Can you please play the footage, after which I'm going to put some questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: From the beginning or from that point we have seen? From the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. From the beginning would be better so that we don't lose continuity, so that we can see that the frame that we looked at is an integral part of the footage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise because of the length of the video footage. This was footage of a column that was over 5 kilometres long. You could see weapons and people. I would just like to put a few more questions to the witness about this column. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Sir, Witness, did you recognise any of the persons in this column, and is this footage of the column recorded after the breakthrough?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise anyone. I wasn't there. I don't even know where this was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are these persons from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask them. I don't know whether they are from Srebrenica, or Bratunac, or Visegrad, or Vlasenica, or Zepa, or Rogatica. I didn't ask them. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please answer this: In your estimate, once you've seen this footage, are these able-bodied men who are subject to military service?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen more people there under 18 than over 18. There were children also, I mean young men of 17 or 18 years of age. You can also see women there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Your commander, in his statement, did tell us how many women there were. There were 10 women, according to him. By freezing these frames, we can count the number of persons and weapons. Did you see these people carrying weapons? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had they not had weapons, they wouldn't have been able to pass through. They passed through because they had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do civilians carry weapons as well, or do only military personnel have them?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, there are civilians and people in military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to ask the Trial Chamber to photograph this witness because of his testimony. Perhaps the Prosecution can take a photograph of the witness. He's testifying publicly. We will have other witnesses. Perhaps it would be good to have a photograph of this witness, in the same way that one makes a photograph for a passport or an ID. I apologise to the interpreters. I'm going to repeat. I would like to ask for this witness to be photographed so that the Defence could carry out the required expertise. Perhaps the Prosecution can make a photograph of this witness. He's testifying in public. We're probably going to have video footage from this trial as well. We are of the opinion, however, that an expertise will be the most efficient and most complete way, if we manage to do it with the help of a photograph such as ones that are taken for a passport or an ID card. The Defence will not make early conclusions, but we do have to make the adequate proofs that will be useful in the coming stages of the trial in order to confirm the basic suspicions or to remove all suspicions. Thank you very much. May I have a decision about this from the Trial Chamber, a decision on this request? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just two brief points, Mr. President, and good afternoon. The first is that General Tolimir may not be aware of this, but the proceedings are being videotaped, so there is a bank of videotape for every witness that's available. Should, for whatever reason, the Defence require a video still, that can be done. So I don't think we need to engage in expert photography to accomplish the request that General Tolimir has. I think we have the resources already at hand from the video booth. Secondly, and this ties into Prosecution's question about exactly where General Tolimir is going with this line of questioning, that ties in, I presume, to his request for this photograph. I don't think it's any secret that what General Tolimir wants to do is compare a photograph of the witness to the photographic still that he has shown to the Trial Chamber. If that is General Tolimir's position, then, under Rule 90, I think the witness, to be fair to the witness, should have the general's case put to him. And we, frankly, are unsure of what the general's case is, and thus what the point of this particular line of cross-examination is. If it's the general's position that this witness was not at the Orahovac execution site and is lying about being at the Orahovac execution site on the 14th of July, because, according to the general, he's in Nezuk on the 16th of July, he should put that proposition to the witness and allow the witness the opportunity to answer the question. If the general has another theory, then that should be put to the witness as well, to be fair to the witness and to comply with Rule 90. And, again, these two issues, I think, tie to each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you have heard what the Prosecutor said. The parties and the Chamber has access to the tape, the videotape of these recordings, and you can take one part of that. Then we have a picture of the witness. I think you could be satisfied, but I would like to ask you if you are satisfied with this provision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I said, for the transcript, a moment ago that we do have and will have the videotape, but our expert advised that the easiest way to produce an expertise is to actually have a photograph that is of the same quality as the photographs used for passports or IDs. So I would appreciate it if that kind of photo could be taken of this witness for those purposes. And I leave it to you to decide. But as I've already said, neither I, nor my Defence, have any intention of claiming anything here, but we just want to have this expertise done. And I would thank you for -- and I also would like to thank my learned colleague for the information that he has provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: As this is a quite unusual request, we would propose that you make a written submission, and then we can deal with that in the proper way. But for the moment, as you can see here, I just received a photo from the videotape, very good quality. But for the moment, we won't decide any further about this topic. If you are really interested in that, we would look for such a submission by you. Please carry on with your questioning, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We will do as instructed by you, and we will submit a written motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, on this tape we heard one BH Army member say, and that's at 1.31 through 1.34, where he says: "We have ammunition, and we have everything." And here, before this Trial Chamber, you actually claimed that there were few weapons in Srebrenica, and that had there been any weapons, Srebrenica would not have fallen; is that correct? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But what the soldier is saying here is something that he's saying in the free territory of Tuzla, and I didn't even see who it was exactly who said that. It could have been one of the Tuzla soldiers. They were in the free territory, and perhaps there were weapons there. But in Srebrenica, there were no weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I just wanted to hear from you, whether you, too, heard that. And on line 33 [as interpreted], line 21 and 22, you said: "I don't know how Srebrenica fell or how Srebrenica could have fallen if we had had all these weapons." Thank you. Now, since you also, during your testimony here, claimed that you are well acquainted with different types of weapons, could you please tell us what kind of weapons you could actually observe carried by the men in this column. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could see there were semi-automatic rifles and one M-53 machine-gun, and there were also some hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please see the tape, 9 minutes, 41 seconds. Thank you. At 9 minutes, 41 seconds. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, this individual wearing the red T-shirt, what is the weapon that he is carrying? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a PM.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: That is short for what? Could you tell the Trial Chamber what the name of this weapon is? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you tell us, please, while you were watching this video-clip, could you tell us, what are the weapons carried by the people around this individual in the red T-shirt? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can only see an automatic rifle, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But a moment ago, when you looked at this video-clip --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, maybe every third or fourth or fifth person actually carries a gun, but you can see it here as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness the video-clip at 1 minute, 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, you saw this a moment ago. What kind of weapons are these men carrying?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are these army or military weapons, or are they weapons that would be carried by civilians hunting?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't see any civilians here. I see soldiers or troops from Tuzla, and they are armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a clip of this column that had managed to break through; correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Trial Chamber please admit the video-clip we've just seen into evidence, to admit it into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it that you received this from the Prosecution. It was disclosed to you? Perhaps, Mr. Thayer, you can give us some information.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. As I think the witness has already testified, and as the Trial Chamber, itself, has seen, this footage has been disclosed to the Defence in various forms. Some of this footage was seen by the Trial Chamber a couple of days ago, and it does depict the movement of the column into the free area of Nezuk on or about the 16th of July. So you've seen portions of it a couple of days ago. You're seeing some of the same portions and some other portions today. But that's what we have, Nezuk troops and then the column coming up to meet them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The portions we have seen today will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D15, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, and I thank my learned colleague for his explanation. And I have another question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In your testimony in the Popovic case, on page 297 you say that Srebrenica was attacked and that people were mobilised in order to defend it. When Srebrenica was attacked, people mobilised again in order to defend themselves. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I probably did. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Would you tell us, please, how many men were mobilised in Srebrenica, if you know, and for how many days was the fighting around Srebrenica going on?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the number. I was not the one who mobilised them. But as I've already said, the fighting lasted about seven days, or, actually, the shelling of Srebrenica lasted about seven days. But I didn't mobilise those men, so I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me, please, is it possible to sustain fighting for seven days without having adequate weapons?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was no fighting, really. It was just shelling. They were shelling the town with artillery weapons. They never even tried to enter Srebrenica. And once our troops broke through, then, well, they entered Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter kindly requests that the accused repeats his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir and Mr. Oric, you're still overlapping many times so that the interpreters can't catch what you are saying. Please repeat your last question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would like Mr. Oric to tell the Trial Chamber whether he knows whether there were any places where the lines have been broken through around Srebrenica, other than along the axis where he said that they intervened near Crveni [as interpreted] Jadar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in the territory where I was and where I lived, there were no -- there was no shifting of the line; only around UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us, please, Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to make the record clear in the future, I note that in the transcript there is a question about a location in General Tolimir's question. It's been recorded as "Crveni Jadar." I suspect that's not the location that General Tolimir had in mind, and it may be a transcription problem, but we need to, I think, clarify it just for the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please clarify that, on the request of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You can check the transcript, but I said "Zeleni Jadar," whether any other front-lines had been breached except at Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And could the witness please repeat his answer for the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could now the witness tell us if he knows whether any of the civilians, women or children, were captured in villages around Srebrenica or in Srebrenica by the Serb Army. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my territory, there were no such instances.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please pull up D1, page 8. In English, that would be on page 10. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You can see here in the first paragraph, line 8 -- in English, that's page 10, and in Serbian, page 8, document D1. Thank you. ERN number 0185-4526. In Serbian, that's the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the Chamber would be appreciative if you could tell us what kind of document is it, what we have on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is an order issued by the deputy commander of Naser Oric, Ramiz, issued to the sabotage -- actually, this is his statement, and he states that he issued a task to the sabotage units, a member of which the witness was too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript and for a better understanding of what you are putting to the witness, it would be helpful if we always could see the first page of the document and then the relevant page you want to deal with. Could we perhaps see the first page of this document first. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just ask the witness to take his headphones off just for a brief moment, please. Just two things. Mr. President, yes, this is a statement of Ramiz Becirovic. We've seen this before. Mr. Becirovic is no longer living, just to clarify that. Secondly, and I think we've been pretty flexible about these kinds of objections before, but embedded in the general's question to this witness was that the -- the suggestion that he was the commander of a sabotage unit, and we've heard, again I think a couple of times, that that is not the case; that he was the commander of a squad of 10 men. And I wanted the witness to take off his headphones, but if the general has a basis for that, then fine, but that question should be put directly to the witness as a proposition and not sort of embedded as part of another question, because that has been an issue in the past. And I just note that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, you can take your earphones again. And from the impression that the witness understood what you were talking about, Mr. Thayer: Mr. Tolimir, in the way that you are putting questions to the witness, please be careful. It could be sometimes understood as a leading question. And take into account what Mr. Thayer has just explained. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I was just reading the statements in the Popovic case, where a gentleman was responding to the questions, and when he was quoted something from Slobodna Dalmacija.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was quoted to him by a member of the Popovic Defence, whether he was in the sabotage unit, and he said that he was. And here I can read a part of his statement where he admitted in the newspapers, in the interview, that he was a commander of a sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you should put questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, sir, did you give a statement to "Slobodna Dalmacija," and did you state in that interview or statement that you were a commander of a sabotage unit?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if I did or not. And journalists can write what they wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, here I'm going to read it to you. Since you don't recall, I'm going to read back to you what you said, and you can say whether you said it or not. Thank you. I quote --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please tell us where he's reading from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading from the "Nedina [phoen] Dalmacija." It's an interview given to "Slobodna Dalmacija," the Sunday edition, which is an exhibit in the Popovic case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note, we do not have that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I repeat: "On the eve of the fall of Srebrenica, I received an order, in view of the fact that I was the commander of a sabotage squad, to guard the UNPROFOR base above the villages of Jaglici and Susnjari. Namely, the UNPROFOR members tried to escape, and we were returning them back to the base with our Zoljas." Thank you, I am finished with my quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, sir, do you recall giving such a statement, and do you recall confirming that in the Popovic case? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I don't recall that, and journalists can write whatever they want. Whatever is easier for them, that's how they will write.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to remind you of another one of your statements in that same interview, in the same interview, where you say: "I spent about a month in Tuzla. We picked up 47 people who were carrying medicines and were going back to Srebrenica; Nurif Rizvanovic had 500 armed men, and he set off with us. Nurif was later liquidated by our men because it was assumed that he was a Serbian spy." Do you recall that statement? Do you remember that statement? You also mentioned that in the transcript in the Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember stating that, and to whom. And as for Nurif, Nurif did not come with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You said that in the same interview that I referred to. I just read back to you a little bit what you said before so that you can recognise your own interview. And you also said, in a trial here, that you went to get a doctor. Didn't you say that, you went to get the doctor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know I went to get a doctor, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Well, I see Mr. Thayer is wanting to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think if the witness is going to be questioned about an interview or a document, he should have the opportunity to look at it. This was not on the list of exhibits. We're not going to stand on absolute formality. We know sometimes there are exhibits that are going to come out on an examination that maybe we don't have notice of. But if we are going to be showing the witness an interview and quote from parts of it, then I think the witness should have an opportunity to take a look at it and see whether he remembers it, whether he's got familiarity with it, and then be able to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it that the Prosecution was not notified about the use of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I understand that things unfold during the course of a cross, but just to be fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You have it as a hard copy. We are, we were told, an e-court chamber, and the procedure should be followed. Please carry on. I think it's not necessary for your questions to put these quotations to the witness. Just carry on asking questions, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I can give this for the witness to look at. There is an ERN number on this piece of paper as well. The Prosecutor can also look at it. I can provide it so that the witness can see what that is. I apologise to the Prosecutor. Thank you. I would like to carry on with my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If that is in e-court, it could be called up on the screen. If not, I think that is not the proper way because then, in that case, we don't have the proper record. You should continue your questioning without hard copies.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President. We can move to the commander's order to the 28th Division, received by the sabotage units, if you permit us. We're going to move to the order issued by Ramiz Becirovic, who was the acting commander of the 28th Division before the attack on Srebrenica. Thank you. Thank you. This is document D1, page 8 in the Serbian. In English, it's page 10. Thank you. Can we please see that on the screen so that the witness could look at it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you see page 8 in the Serbian of this document?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. It's not in Serbian. I can see that it is written in the Latinic script.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right. Can you please read that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Because?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The letters are very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you what your commander, Ramiz Becirovic, said in his statement that he gave in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you indicate which part of this very long page you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is the statement given by Ramiz Becirovic on the 11th of August, 1995, in Tuzla. I'm now going to read line 8, in the first paragraph, to line 22. So lines 8 to line 22. Mr. President, may I proceed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, I am quoting from the statement given by Ramiz Becirovic in Tuzla after he came out with the column. I quote: "From the command of the 2nd Corps, from the General Staff, an order was given that sabotage actions should attract the attention of the enemy, and in that way to carry out reconnaissance of the enemy along its depth in order to assist the action to de-blockade Sarajevo. I assigned several groups whose assignment it was to reconnoiter and to fire only if they must, and all the groups carried out their tasks of reconnaissance without combat, and they all returned. One group was going in the direction Kraglivode with the assignment of firing, and that is when they destroyed one weapon and killed three soldiers. One group was infiltrated in Rupovo Brdo, which was also firing and killed four Chetniks. This was all after my return to Srebrenica; namely, in June 1995. I issued the assignment that all sabotage reconnaissance platoons from the Zepa area should go into the Han Pogled and Han Pijesak and Sokolac sectors along the Han Pijesak-Vlasenica road. Pursuant to a decision by the commander of the 285th Brigade, nine groups were formed which were carrying out these assignments. These groups were in combat, and they destroyed about 60 Chetniks, while one group entered the village of Visnjica and set a few houses on fire." Thank you. My question to the witness is: are you aware that sabotage groups were formed by the commander of Srebrenica in order to attack the neighbouring villages from Srebrenica and Zepa, and did this precede the attacks on Srebrenica and Zeleni Jadar? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when this was, but that whole time that you are reading, you are reading "sabotage units." I was not in a sabotage unit. I was in a manoeuvre unit. I don't recall when this happened, in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please explain to the Trial Chamber what the difference was, in your brigade, between a sabotage unit and a manoeuvre unit.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sabotage units carry out sabotage, while manoeuvring units manoeuvre and they cover the area between or among the UNPROFOR bunkers. The area was empty. This is what we were doing. We were preventing the Chetniks from entering that area and breaking through.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Will you tell the Trial Chamber if this unit of yours participated in the attack on the UNPROFOR check-point? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What UNPROFOR attack? That never happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just put this question, whether he took part in the attack on UNPROFOR. Please go ahead. I did not assert anything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, just so we have a clear record, General Tolimir referred to an UNPROFOR attack, and we don't have a month or even a year that's referred to. If he's tying it to the document, then let's please tie it to the document, but it just came out as a general question, and so we have an answer that doesn't really make sense because the question, I think, is just too vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But we have an answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, when you carry on now, please bear in mind that you make clear what you are talking about. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I asked clearly -- I want to tell the Prosecutor that in this question, I was referring to the event of the 11th in Zeleni Jadar about which the previous witness spoke, and this is in the transcript. But if it's necessary to repeat that, no problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's not necessary that you repeat anything in the moment. Just ask questions to this witness. Continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember what these groups did, in terms of what this deputy commander, Ramiz, is talking about in this statement of his from which I read and quoted to you, where he says that in one place 60 persons were killed and that others were destroyed? Is it true what Becirovic, Ramiz, says in his statement of the 11th of August, 1995? I'm talking about events that happened before the fall of Srebrenica and the attack on Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I never heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell me this: Have you heard that your unit had a task -- the following task: To engage from the demilitarised zone against the Republika Srpska Army and the civilian population in order to provide support to the operation that was ongoing around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My manoeuvre unit never was issued any assignment to open fire or anything of that sort, so it is absolutely out of the question that anyone ordered us to shoot. How could we shoot when UNPROFOR was there? That would mean that we would have to actually clash with UNPROFOR. We actually hid our weapons from UNPROFOR in order to be able to maintain that line.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter requests that the accused repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreter did not catch your question because it was again an overlapping. Look on the screen, on the transcript, and you can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, did you take part in capturing the UNPROFOR check-point at Jaglici on the 11th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. UNPROFOR actually fled that check-point, and we just went there in order to keep -- to defend that line. And there was no clash with the UNPROFOR. The women were trying to stop them from leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you actually secure the positions that had been deserted by UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I've just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you heard that an UNPROFOR member was killed in Srebrenica on the 11th of July, and what can you tell us about that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything about it because I don't know. I was not in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I don't think there's going to be any dispute that the death of the UNPROFOR soldier occurred on the 8th of July. I don't think there's any dispute. Unless General Tolimir has some basis to ask a question that there was another UNPROFOR soldier killed on the 11th, I think we either need to correct the record or provide some further information about some killing on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, the accused is not giving evidence. He's putting questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President, but the questions need to have an accurate, I think, basis of fact to be able to put to the witness. And, again, I don't think there's any dispute that there was only one soldier killed, and that was on the 8th. Just so we have a clear, accurate record, again, if there's evidence that somebody was killed on the 11th, then that should be brought out, but -- and I think we're going to be in agreement. I don't know whether it's a slip of the tongue or something else, but if we're talking about the 11th, that's completely new -- a new suggestion that we haven't heard ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. Tolimir, carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, you confirmed in Popovic, on transcript page 977, that at the moment when you surrendered, you had with you -- in fact, that you said that you were a civilian, that you represented yourself as a civilian. Is that correct? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't make any representations. I was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The interpreters don't catch your question if you immediately start your next question before the answer is translated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, would you answer my question. Did you consider yourself to be a civilian only because you were wearing civilian clothes, or were you still -- did you still enjoy the status of a BH soldier?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was in civilian clothes, and I had no weapons. Now, what the interpretation of that would be, that depends on who's interpreting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Tell me, please, did you have any ID on you? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I didn't take anything with me. I was not at home when Srebrenica fell. I was at Jaglici, and that's where I set out from. I didn't even go home before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, tell us, please, was it standard practice in your unit not to carry any IDs on you? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, did your unit actually, as a matter of course, not carry any documents, its members not carry any documents on the day?
